Cooking: 50 minutes | Rating = | Difficulty = 2 | Image = [[Image:Pommes Anna.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]] | [[Cookbook:Side dishes|Side dishes]] '''Potatoes Anna''' (or ''pommes Anna'') is a classic French dish of sliced, layered potatoes cooked in a very large amount of melted butter. It can be eaten hot or cold. ==Ingredients== * 4 [[cookbook:potato|potato]]es, optionally peeled * 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]] ==Equipment== * [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]] * 23 cm round [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie tin]] ==Procedure== # Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 250 °C. # Melt the butter. # [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] the potatoes thinly. Press slices against [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|absorbent paper]] to dry. # [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the tin with melted butter. Layer the potato slices into the tin, brushing each layer with butter and ending with butter on the top. # Cover and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] in the oven for 20 minutes. Uncover and cook for a further 30 minutes.
